Generate private sector ownership data

Source: R/7_health_systems.R
generate_private_sector_data.Rd

Reshapes health system metrics into the share of health facilities that are private, NGO and public in each admin level 1 unit, for plot.cd_private_sector(). The public share is what remains after the private and NGO shares.

Usage

generate_private_sector_data(.data, legend_labels = NULL)

Arguments

.data

Data frame containing subnational health indicators, with the columns adminlevel_1, private_facility_share and ngo_facility_share, such as the output of calculate_health_system_metrics() with admin_level = "adminlevel_1".

legend_labels

(Optional) A named list to override default legend labels (elements Private, NGO and Public).

Value

A tibble of class cd_private_sector with one row per admin level 1 unit and facility type, and the columns adminlevel_1, facility_type (a factor ordered private, NGO, public, with the labels as its levels) and share (percent). The attributes lbl_prv, lbl_ngo and lbl_pub hold the labels used.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core")
data <- load_data(path)
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths,
#>   ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah
metrics <- calculate_health_system_metrics(data, admin_level = "adminlevel_1")

generate_private_sector_data(metrics)
#> # A tibble: 24 × 3
#>    adminlevel_1  facility_type share
#>    <chr>         <fct>         <dbl>
#>  1 Rift Valley   Private        26.4
#>  2 Rift Valley   NGO            13.9
#>  3 Rift Valley   Public         59.6
#>  4 Western       Private        27.6
#>  5 Western       NGO            12.2
#>  6 Western       Public         60.1
#>  7 Eastern       Private        36.6
#>  8 Eastern       NGO            12.6
#>  9 Eastern       Public         50.9
#> 10 North Eastern Private        27.1
#> # ℹ 14 more rows

# with another label in the legend
shares <- generate_private_sector_data(metrics, legend_labels = list(Private = "For profit"))
plot(shares)
